developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_automated_backups_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-5 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_high_availability_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-6 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-7 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Server"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Server: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0031"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-server", label: "Hetzner Cloud Server", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_audit_telemetry_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-8 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_tls_enforcement_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-9 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_private_networking_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-10 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Server"]

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0034"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-server", label: "Hetzner Cloud Server", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_firewall_whitelist_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-11 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_ssh_key_only_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-12 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_automated_backups_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-1 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Server"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Server: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0037"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-server", label: "Hetzner Cloud Server", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_high_availability_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-2 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_storage_encryption_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-3 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_audit_telemetry_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-4 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Server"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Server: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0040"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-server", label: "Hetzner Cloud Server", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_tls_enforcement_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-5 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_private_networking_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-6 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_server.hetzner_server_firewall_whitelist_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Server: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-7 Cloud Compute Servers (CX/CPX/CAX))
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Server
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud server list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Server"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Server: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0043"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-server", label: "Hetzner Cloud Server", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_tls_enforcement_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-1 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_private_networking_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-2 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_firewall_whitelist_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-3 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Network"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Network: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0046"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-network", label: "Hetzner Cloud Network", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_ssh_key_only_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-4 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

An endpoint reachable from the test environment

tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.

aws configure list

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_automated_backups_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-5 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-6 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-7 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Network"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Network: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0050"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-network", label: "Hetzner Cloud Network", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

hcloud context active
aws configure list

checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_audit_telemetry_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-8 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_tls_enforcement_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-9 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_private_networking_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-10 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_firewall_whitelist_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-11 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

An endpoint reachable from the test environment

tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_ssh_key_only_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-12 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_automated_backups_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-1 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_high_availability_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-2 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud network list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Network"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Network: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0057"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-network", label: "Hetzner Cloud Network", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_network.hetzner_network_storage_encryption_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Network: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-3 Private Networks & vSwitch Interconnect)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Network
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
