threat_model.attack_vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_audit_telemetry_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-8 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Firewall"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0094"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-firewall", label: "Hetzner Cloud Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_tls_enforcement_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-9 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_private_networking_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-10 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

hcloud context active
aws configure list

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_firewall_whitelist_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-11 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_ssh_key_only_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-12 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Firewall"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0098"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-firewall", label: "Hetzner Cloud Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_automated_backups_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-1 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_high_availability_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-2 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

An endpoint reachable from the test environment

aws configure list

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_storage_encryption_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-3 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_audit_telemetry_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-4 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Firewall"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0102"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-firewall", label: "Hetzner Cloud Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_tls_enforcement_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-5 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_private_networking_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-6 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

hcloud context active
aws configure list

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_firewall_whitelist_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-7 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_ssh_key_only_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-8 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Firewall"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0106"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-firewall", label: "Hetzner Cloud Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_automated_backups_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-9 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-10 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_storage_encryption_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-11 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_audit_telemetry_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-12 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Firewall"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0110"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-firewall", label: "Hetzner Cloud Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_tls_enforcement_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-1 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_private_networking_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-2 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

hcloud context active
aws configure list

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_firewall_whitelist_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-3 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_ssh_key_only_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-4 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Firewall"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0114"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-firewall", label: "Hetzner Cloud Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

An endpoint reachable from the test environment

Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.

failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_automated_backups_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-5 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_high_availability_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-6 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-7 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_audit_telemetry_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-8 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Firewall"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0118"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-firewall", label: "Hetzner Cloud Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_tls_enforcement_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-9 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_private_networking_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-10 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

hcloud context active
aws configure list

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_firewall_whitelist_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-11 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_ssh_key_only_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-12 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Firewall"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0122"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-firewall", label: "Hetzner Cloud Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

An endpoint reachable from the test environment

Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_automated_backups_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-1 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_high_availability_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-2 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

aws configure list

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_storage_encryption_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-3 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_audit_telemetry_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-4 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner Cloud Firewall"]
      requirement["Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0126"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-firewall", label: "Hetzner Cloud Firewall", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_tls_enforcement_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-5 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application connectivity and network policy
developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_private_networking_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-6 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

hcloud context active
aws configure list

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_firewall.hetzner_firewall_firewall_whitelist_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner Cloud Firewall: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-7 Stateful Cloud Firewalls & Rule Sets)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner Cloud Firewall
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud firewall list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Source, destination, route, protocol, port and DNS resolution
dependencies: Application subnets or endpoints with a defined route
Explicit ingress and egress rules
An endpoint reachable from the test environment
steps: Create address ranges, routes and any required private endpoint.
Configure forwarding and filtering independently of application identity.
Run allowed and blocked connection tests from the actual application network.
tests: Resolve the endpoint from the application environment.
Verify allowed traffic succeeds and a denied source or port fails.
failures: DNS failure: check private zone links and resolver configuration.
Connection timeout: inspect routes, firewall rules and endpoint state.

hcloud context active
aws configure list

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
