developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_private_networking_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-2 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_firewall_whitelist_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-3 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_ssh_key_only_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-4 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_automated_backups_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-5 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner API Tokens"]
      requirement["Hetzner API Tokens: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0693"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_high_availability_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-6 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-7 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_audit_telemetry_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-8 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner API Tokens"]
      requirement["Hetzner API Tokens: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0696"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_tls_enforcement_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-9 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_private_networking_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-10 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_firewall_whitelist_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-11 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_ssh_key_only_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-12 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_automated_backups_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-1 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_high_availability_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-2 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_storage_encryption_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-3 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner API Tokens"]
      requirement["Hetzner API Tokens: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0703"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_audit_telemetry_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-4 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_tls_enforcement_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-5 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_private_networking_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-6 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner API Tokens"]
      requirement["Hetzner API Tokens: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0706"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_firewall_whitelist_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-7 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_ssh_key_only_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-8 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_automated_backups_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-9 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_high_availability_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-10 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_storage_encryption_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-11 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_audit_telemetry_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Mandate Real-Time Action Log Collection & Telemetry (Tier-12 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_network"
  not r.change.after.metrics
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure metrics for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_tls_enforcement_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-1 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_load_balancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure tls_enabled for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Hetzner Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Hetzner API Tokens"]
      requirement["Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API token and project permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: HTZ-BP-0713"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Hetzner Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-iam", label: "Hetzner API Tokens", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:hetzner-audit", label: "Hetzner Cloud action log and audit trail", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_private_networking_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-2 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure network_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_firewall_whitelist_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-3 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_firewall"
  not r.change.after.rules
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure rules for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
threat_model.defense_barrier: Hetzner Cloud Firewall Rule Filter & Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_ssh_key_only_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce ED25519 SSH Key Authentication without Passwords (Tier-4 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, EU Sovereign Cloud
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_ssh_key"
  not r.change.after.public_key
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure public_key for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_automated_backups_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Mandate Daily Automated Backup Schedules (Tier-5 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.backups
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure backups for compliance standard ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_high_availability_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enforce Anti-Affinity Spread in Placement Groups (Tier-6 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_server"
  not r.change.after.placement_group_id
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure placement_group_id for compliance standard CIS Hetzner Linux Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Workload authentication and API authorization
developer_guide.contract: Issuer, subject, audience, role scope and token lifetime
dependencies: An explicitly trusted identity issuer or workload principal
A target API and a minimal permission set
steps: Register the workload identity and its trust conditions.
Bind the smallest resource and action scope.
Exchange identity evidence for short-lived credentials through the supported SDK.
tests: Call the permitted action with the intended principal.
Reject an unexpected audience, expired credential and out-of-scope resource.
failures: Authentication failure: check issuer, audience, clock skew and trust conditions.
Access denied: inspect effective permissions and applicable explicit denies.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
hcloud context active
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package hetzner.hetzner_iam.hetzner_iam_storage_encryption_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Hetzner API Tokens: Enable Storage Box Encrypted Subaccounts & ZFS Snapshots (Tier-7 Project Scoped API Tokens & RBAC)
# Compliance: BSI C5 Cloud Standard, SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Remote brute-force or unauthorized packet ingress targeting Hetzner API Tokens
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "hcloud_volume"
  not r.change.after.encryption
  msg := sprintf("Hetzner resource %v must configure encryption for compliance standard BSI C5 Cloud Standard", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Hetzner CLI: hcloud iam list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
